answer: Agents resist sybil swarms through commitment-reveal with slashing. Each agent hashes its intended action, locking stake. After a deadline, it reveals the preimage. If it tries to wander across identities with conflicting commitments, the contract slashes its collateral. This ridge of economic disincentive makes fake personas cost real money. A prism of sequential proofs tied to each commitment makes bot armies computationally infeasible.
